summary: This component renders a blog post item that adapts its appearance depending on whether you're viewing a single post or browsing a list of posts. It conditionally shows certain interactive elements like AI badges, article actions, and engagement features only when viewing the full post page, while adding spacing when the post appears as a card in a list.

explanations.22: This helper function checks whether we're on the individual post page or viewing a list of posts, and returns a CSS class name only for list view to add bottom spacing between post cards.
explanations.24: The ternary operator returns the margin class if NOT on the post page (meaning we're in list view), otherwise returns undefined so no extra spacing is added on the full post page.
explanations.28: We're calling a Docusaurus hook that gives us info about whether this component is rendering as a full post page or as a preview card in a list.
explanations.29: We're extracting the frontMatter object from metadata—this contains custom fields from the blog post's YAML header like whether it's AI-assisted.
explanations.31: This conditionally renders the AI icon badge only if two things are true: the post is marked as AI-assisted AND we're viewing the full post page (not a list card).
explanations.34: Article actions (like share buttons) only make sense to show on the full post page, not on preview cards, so we conditionally create this element.
explanations.38: clsx is a utility that combines multiple CSS class names together, ignoring undefined values—here we're merging the container spacing class with any additional classes passed to this component.
explanations.44: The && operator is a common React pattern: if isBlogPostPage is true, render everything inside the fragment; if false, render nothing.
explanations.57: This checks if tried_it is explicitly set to false in frontMatter—if it's not false (meaning it's true or undefined), render the TriedIt component.
